articles.title: ChronoCulture: Evaluating Cultural Awareness Across Time in Large Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.20472v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cultural attitudes and social norms evolve over time, yet most cultural benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) treat culture as a static attribute of a country or region. We introduce ChronoCulture, a benchmark of 10,360 temporal pairs built from longitudinal survey data across 72 countries. Each pair contains the same survey question asked in the same country in an older and a newer year, with full population response distributions as ground truth. articles.title: Partitioning Israeli Municipalities into Politically Homogeneous Cantons: A Constrained Spatial Clustering Approach
articles.summary: arXiv:2603.11805v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Israeli society has experienced significant political polarization in recent years, reflected in five Knesset elections held within a four-year period (2019-2022). Public discourse increasingly references hypothetical divisions of the country into politically homogeneous "cantons." This paper develops a data-driven algorithmic approach to explore such divisions using publicly available municipality-level election results and geographic boundary data. articles.title: Mapping data literacy trajectories in K-12 education
articles.summary: arXiv:2603.28317v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Data literacy skills are fundamental in computer science education. However, understanding how data-driven systems work represents a paradigm shift from traditional rule-based programming. We conducted a systematic literature review of 84 studies to understand K-12 learners' engagement with data across disciplines and contexts. We propose the data paradigms framework that categorises learning activities along two dimensions: (i) logic (knowledge-based or data-driven systems), and (ii) explainability (transparent or opaque models). articles.title: Fake Plastic Voters: When Political Parties Can Use AI-Simulated Focus Groups
articles.summary: arXiv:2606.00043v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Political parties strive to understand their electorates, and focus groups are a vital tool in these efforts. AI-enhanced simulation technologies (AESTs) enable synthetic focus groups in a fraction of the time (and cost), raising the question of when and how such simulated evidence can be used in campaign research. This paper develops a decision matrix to help party strategists match research needs to appropriate simulation technologies and to identify when to escalate to hybrid or fully human focus groups. articles.title: A Global View of How LLMs Value Human Time
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.18515v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly act as personal assistants; however, little is known about how they capture national-level preferences on a global scale. Given that "time" is a universal and representative concept, we examine LLMs' time preferences by varying only users' country and measuring the compensation LLMs deem appropriate for a 60-minute appointment delay. articles.summary: arXiv:2603.28916v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Passing actions are commonly evaluated through ball progression and attacking outcomes, yet their relationship with the spatial organisation of the opposition provides an additional perspective on passing behaviour. articles.title: How Far Are We From True Auto-Research?
articles.summary: arXiv:2605.19156v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent auto-research systems can produce complete papers, but feasibility is not the same as quality, and the field still lacks a systematic study of how good agent-generated papers actually are. articles.title: DeTox-Fed: Detecting Toxic Conversations in the Fediverse with Federated Graph Neural Networks
articles.summary: arXiv:2605.21054v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The rise of decentralized social networks (DSNs), and in particular the rapid uptake of the Fediverse (e.g., Pleroma, Mastodon, Lemmygrad), introduces new challenges in content moderation. Independent instances host their own data, follow different moderation policies, and often observe only partial views of conversations. We present DeTox-Fed, a federated graph-learning framework for detecting toxic conversations in DSNs without requiring instances to share raw conversations or moderation labels. articles.summary: arXiv:2607.01244v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The growing number and complexity of technical regulations represent an important challenge for all professionals in regulated industries.
